transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what brings you in to see me?

I came in because... well, I just can't shake this certainty that I'm being punished. It's about my father. I feel like I'm being punished for letting his health decline. My sister tries to talk me out of it, and she even shows me the doctor's notes or tells me that I've done everything right, but it doesn't change anything for me. It just feels like some kind of judgment has already been passed on me, and I don't know how to get past it.
Besides this feeling of being punished, have you noticed that your mood has been consistently down or that you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes, I have. Most days, I just wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It's like... the color has just gone out of everything. I can sit at my desk at work in HR, or I'll just be staring at the garden beds at home, and I feel like none of it reaches me anymore. I just feel very down.
Has this feeling of being punished ever been present even during times when your mood was not low, or does it only occur alongside these periods of depression?

No, it's only alongside this. Before this depression really settled in around my father's decline, I never believed I was being punished. I never heard voices or anything like that before this, either. It was really only after... I don't know, maybe a few months of just feeling so low and guilty and completely worn down that those experiences started happening. So, no, never when my mood was normal.

Before this period tied to your father's decline, have you ever had another separate episode in your life where you felt this same kind of深度 low mood and hopelessness for weeks or more, followed by a return to your normal self?

No, I haven't. I mean... I've had stressful times at work, or just normal bad days, but nothing like this. I've never had a period where I felt this kind of deep hopelessness for weeks on end before everything happened with my dad. This is really the first time I've ever gone through something like this.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-ever major depressive episode characterized by persistent low mood, anhedonia, and a pervasive sense of hopelessness triggered by her father's declining health. Superimposed on this depressive episode are mood-congruent psychotic features—specifically a fixed, delusional belief that she is being 'punished' for her father's decline, which persists despite reassurance and contrary evidence from her sister (delusion of guilt/punishment). These psychotic symptoms emerged only after several months of depressive symptoms and are absent when her mood is euthymic, confirming they are mood-congruent and secondary to the depressive episode rather than an independent psychotic disorder. There is no history of prior manic/hypomanic episodes or prior depressive episodes, ruling out bipolar disorder and recurrent depressive disorder. The absence of psychotic symptoms outside of mood episodes rules out schizoaffective disorder. This presentation meets criteria for Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, Severe, with Psychotic Symptoms (F32.3).
